facts.statement: The species Hongshanopterus lacustris was named and described in 2008 by Wang Xiaolin, Diogenes de Almeida Campos, Zhou Zhonghe, and Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner.
facts.quote: The type species Hongshanopterus lacustris was in 2008 named and described by Wang Xiaolin, Diogenes de Almeida Campos, Zhou Zhonghe and Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner.

facts.statement: Hongshanopterus lived in the Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Hongshanopterus is a genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: The estimated wingspan of Hongshanopterus was between 1.8 and 1.9 meters.
facts.quote: The wingspan of Hongshanopterus was estimated at 1.8 to 1.9 meters.

facts.statement: Hongshanopterus possessed about thirty-six teeth in its upper jaws combined.
facts.quote: It possessed a relatively high number of teeth, about thirty-six for both upper jaws combined.

facts.statement: The teeth of Hongshanopterus were robust with triangular crowns that were flattened from the mouth side to the lip side.
facts.quote: The teeth were robust and had triangular crowns which were flattened from mouth side to "lip" side, like those of other istiodactylids.

facts.statement: Hongshanopterus had a ridge on the underside of its pterygoid bone that pointed obliquely to the front and outside.
facts.quote: The pterygoid bone had a ridge at the underside, pointing obliquely to the front and the outside.

facts.statement: In 2008, Hongshanopterus was placed in the family Istiodactylidae in a basal position.
facts.quote: Hongshanopterus was in 2008 placed in the Istiodactylidae, in a basal position.

facts.statement: Hongshanopterus is classified in the family Istiodactylidae, though this classification is sometimes questioned.
Hongshanopterus lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

rejected.quote: It was less derived than other istiodactylids by having a tooth row that extended beyond the first third of the skull, and by having some teeth that were directed backwards.

rejected.statement: Analyses by Kellner et al. (2019) recovered Hongshanopterus as the sister taxon of the family Istiodactylidae within the group Istiodactyliformes.
rejected.quote: In the analyses, they recovered Hongshanopterus as the sister taxon of the family Istiodactylidae, and placed within the more inclusive group Istiodactyliformes.
